Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 6) demonstrates a small, hypoplastic right lung with diffuse opacity and volume loss, resulting in dextroposition (rightward shift) of the heart and mediastinum. These are the classic radiographic hallmarks of Scimitar syndrome (congenital pulmonary venolobar syndrome), often accompanied by absence or hypoplasia of the right upper lobe and an anomalous vein (scimitar sign).
